settings.answer_1: Fill the dropper to the line and release it under your tongue. Hold it there for 60 seconds, then swallow. Once a day, ideally with your morning routine. One bottle is 30 servings.
settings.question_2: Why under the tongue instead of a capsule?
settings.answer_2: The pigments in MacuDrops are micellized in MCT oil and sunflower lecithin, so they’re already dispersed when they reach the thin tissue under your tongue. A capsule has to break down in your stomach first, and fat-soluble carotenoids like lutein are known to absorb poorly that way.
settings.question_3: Can I take it alongside my eye treatments?
settings.answer_3: MacuDrops is a dietary supplement. It does not replace injections, laser or any treatment your eye doctor prescribes. Keep every appointment. Show your ophthalmologist the ingredient list, especially if you take blood thinners, because ginkgo biloba can affect bleeding.
settings.answer_4: Lutein 20mg, zeaxanthin 2mg, meso-zeaxanthin 2mg, astaxanthin 4mg, saffron extract 10mg, zinc 10mg and ginkgo biloba 40mg (standardized 24%). Base: MCT oil, sunflower lecithin, natural flavoring.

settings.description_text: Take MacuDrops every day for up to 60 days. If you’re not satisfied for any reason, contact us for a full refund. No questions asked.

settings.question: How long until I notice anything?
settings.answer: Macular pigment builds gradually. Research on lutein and zeaxanthin usually measures changes over 3 to 6 months of daily use, so we recommend giving MacuDrops at least 3 months.*

settings.question: Does MacuDrops replace my eye injections or laser treatment?
settings.answer: No. MacuDrops is a dietary supplement, not a treatment for any eye disease. If you have diabetic retinopathy, macular degeneration or any other eye condition, keep every appointment and follow your eye doctor’s treatment plan.

settings.question: Is it safe with my medications?
settings.answer: Show the ingredient list to your doctor before starting, especially if you take blood thinners (warfarin, aspirin, clopidogrel), because ginkgo biloba can affect bleeding. Ask your doctor if you are pregnant or nursing.

settings.question: Why drops instead of capsules?
settings.answer: Lutein and the other carotenoids are fat-soluble. In MacuDrops they’re micellized in MCT oil and sunflower lecithin and taken under the tongue, so there’s no capsule to dissolve first.

settings.question: How do I take it?
settings.answer: One dropper under the tongue, hold for 60 seconds, then swallow. Once a day. Each bottle has 30 servings.

settings.question: Where is it made?
settings.answer: In small batches in Japan, in an FDA-registered, GMP-certified facility. Every batch is third-party tested.

settings.question: What if it isn’t for me?
settings.answer: You’re covered by our 60-day money-back guarantee. Contact our team for a full refund.
